correctness.rationale: The cyclic spacings are uniform Dirichlet. The one-coordinate tail \((1-u)^{n-1}\) and two-coordinate tail \((1-u-v)_+^{n-1}\), integrated by layer cake, yield every mixed moment, including the \(n=2\) edge case. Algebra gives the exact covariance. Differentiating \(B_n\) yields the logarithmic derivative \((1-2ns)/[(1-2s)(1-s)]\) for its controlling ratio; its increase/decrease proves uniqueness of the sign threshold. The \(n=2\) polynomial factors and the \(s\ge1/2\) sign follow directly. Uniform exponential expansions and the third-derivative argument establish the limiting equation and uniqueness. The packed checker passed 5,434 checks of exact rational identities, sign profiles, root convergence and independent circle-coordinate simulations.

originality.rationale: The proposed point of originality is the complete finite-n classification that a natural gap-count/covered-fraction covariance has exactly one positive sign-change threshold, plus identification of the limiting critical intensity. Known full joint laws imply access to the covariance, so no originality is asserted for the underlying joint distribution or its mixed moments. Source texts and indexed finding searches did not locate this explicit all-n sign diagram; an inaccessible historical joint-limit paper leaves a residual risk, not a claim of certified priority.

value.rationale: Gap count and covered measure are elementary yet distinct physically meaningful observables of spatial fragmentation. Their covariance reverses sign despite monotone individual coverage and gap behavior, and the theorem proves an all-n unique transition with a nontrivial asymptotic critical intensity. This complete natural parameter classification adds meaningful insight to known joint-coverage information rather than a one-off table value.
